quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #19
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When is highway pavement most slippery?

options.text: After it has been raining for several hours.
When rain first starts.
After it has been raining for one to two hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: When rain first starts.
questions.explanation: Pavement is most slippery when rain first begins. Dirt and oil on the road mix with rainwater to create a slick surface.

questions.question: This white sign means you should not pass other vehicles:

options.text: Until after you pass the sign.
Unless it seems safe to do so.
For any reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: For any reason.
questions.explanation: A white rectangular sign means you must obey the rule. This sign means do not pass other vehicles at any time.

questions.question: If you see a pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane, what should you do?

options.text: The pedestrian must yield the right-of-way.
You must yield the right-of-way.
Honk your horn to let them know you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: A white cane or guide dog shows that a person is blind or has low vision. You must yield the right-of-way to these pedestrians.

questions.question: To turn left from a multilane one-way street onto another one-way street, start your turn from:

options.text: Any lane (as long as it is safe).
The lane closest to the left curb.
The center lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to the left curb.
questions.explanation: When turning left from a one-way street onto another one-way street, start from the far left lane.

questions.question: How should you make room for cars entering the freeway?

options.text: Slow down.
Move to a different lane.
Keep your speed and position the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a different lane.
questions.explanation: Make room for vehicles entering the freeway. Merge into the next lane if possible to create a gap. If you cannot merge, slow down to let them enter safely.

questions.question: You cannot park within ____ of a fire hydrant.

options.text: 25 feet
15 feet
30 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 15 feet
questions.explanation: Do not park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant. Park only in legal spots where other drivers can see your car.

questions.question: If the road ahead is covered in heavy smoke, what should you do?

options.text: Turn on your four-way flashers and keep driving.
Slow down, move right, and stop off the road.
Turn on your high beams and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move right, and stop off the road.
questions.explanation: If heavy smoke covers the road ahead, slow down right away. Drive as far right as you can and stop off the roadway. Then check if it is safe to continue. Some smoke can harm your eyes, lungs, or be deadly.

questions.question: When turning left from a two-way street, where should you position your car?

options.text: Near the right-hand edge of the road.
Near the centerline.
On the left side of the centerline.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the centerline.
questions.explanation: When turning left from a two-way street, stay in the lane closest to the centerline. Turn just before your car reaches the center of the intersection. Do not cut the corner. Turn into the first available legal lane.

questions.question: What does this sign tell you?

options.text: The distance from the road to a bridge or overpass.
The maximum height a vehicle can be in this state.
The maximum width a vehicle can be on the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: The distance from the road to a bridge or overpass.
questions.explanation: This is a low clearance warning sign. It shows how high the space is from the road surface to the bottom of a bridge or overpass (in this case, 12 feet 6 inches).

questions.question: Your car can hydroplane at speeds as low as:

options.text: 45 miles per hour.
35 miles per hour.
40 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: 35 miles per hour.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when water covers the road. Most tires can push water away up to 35 mph. Above 35 mph, tires cannot move the water fast enough. Your tires may lose contact with the road and slide like water skis.

questions.question: You are driving at the speed limit when a traffic light turns yellow. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and drive through the intersection.
Speed up to cross before the light turns red.
Stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely.
questions.explanation: Yellow means the light will turn red soon. Stop safely if you can. If you cannot stop safely, drive through carefully.

questions.question: When should you increase the distance between your vehicle and the vehicle ahead?

options.text: When following a small car.
When another driver is tailgating you.
When you are driving below the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: When another driver is tailgating you.
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, create more space ahead. Slow down gradually or change lanes. Do not brake suddenly.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Steep hill ahead.
The road has curves ahead.
The road is slippery when wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells drivers to be careful in wet weather. The road surface becomes slippery and harder to control.

questions.question: When pulling into traffic from a parked position, you should:

options.text: Drive slower than other traffic for 200 feet.
Wait for a large gap, then speed up to match traffic.
Wait for two vehicles to pass, then enter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for a large gap, then speed up to match traffic.
questions.explanation: Find a gap large enough to safely speed up to match the traffic around you before merging.

questions.question: When parking on a hill, you should:

options.text: Let one rear wheel touch the curb.
Use your parking brake and put the car in "park."
Point your front wheels straight if there is no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your parking brake and put the car in "park."
questions.explanation: Always use the parking brake and shift to "park." Turn your wheels toward the curb on hills to prevent rolling if the brakes fail.

questions.question: At a green arrow, you must:

options.text: Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian still in the intersection.
Yield to pedestrians only.
Wait four seconds before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian still in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can go. First yield to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians in the intersection, then turn in the arrow's direction.

questions.question: At a red light with a green arrow, you may go if:

options.text: You come to a complete stop first.
You wait for the light to change.
You are in the correct lane and the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are in the correct lane and the road is clear.
questions.explanation: If you are in a lane with a green arrow, you may turn in that direction when the road is clear. This works even if the main light is red.

questions.question: When must you show proof of insurance to police?

options.text: Only if you were in a crash.
If you were in a crash or stopped for a ticket.
Only if you were stopped for a ticket.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you were in a crash or stopped for a ticket.
questions.explanation: Always carry proof of insurance. Show it to an officer if you are stopped for any reason or involved in a crash.

questions.question: When turning left onto a one-way street from a two-way street, you should turn into:

options.text: Any lane.
The first lane.
The second lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The first lane.
questions.explanation: Always turn into the first available lane in your direction of travel.

questions.question: When entering an interstate highway, you should:

options.text: Stop, check for cars, and enter when safe.
Check for cars and slow to 25 mph before merging.
Check for cars, speed up to match traffic, and merge when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for cars, speed up to match traffic, and merge when safe.
questions.explanation: Use the entry lane to speed up and match the traffic flow. Then merge smoothly into the highway when there is a gap.

questions.question: You want to turn left at an upcoming corner. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: Other vehicles turning left.
All vehicles coming toward you.
Pedestrians on the sidewalk waiting to walk.

questions.correctAnswerText: All vehicles coming toward you.
questions.explanation: When turning left, you must yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and vehicles moving on their green light.

questions.question: If another car is passing you in a no passing zone, you should:

options.text: Pull off the road.
Keep your speed and position the same.
Slow down so the other car can safely return to your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down so the other car can safely return to your lane.
questions.explanation: Slow down to help the passing vehicle return to your lane safely. This helps everyone avoid hazards ahead.

questions.question: Before entering a curve, you should:

options.text: Turn on your turn signal.
Slow down.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down before curves, hills with poor visibility, slippery roads, and areas with animals or pedestrians. Never drive faster than the speed limit.

questions.question: Which road surface freezes first?

options.text: A tunnel.
An intersection.
A bridge.

questions.correctAnswerText: A bridge.
questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before other road surfaces and thaw after them. Watch for ice on bridges even when other roads are dry.

questions.question: What is the maximum speed to approach a blind intersection?

options.text: 30 mph.
20 mph.
15 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: 15 mph.
questions.explanation: Trees, bushes, or buildings can block your view at a blind intersection. Slow down to no more than 15 mph.

questions.question: Motorcycles, scooters, and mopeds are hard to see. You should:

options.text: Slow down when driving.
Look around constantly.
Share a lane with a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look around constantly.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and can hide in your blind spots. Always look carefully for motorcycles, mopeds, and scooters.

questions.question: When turning or stopping in rain, be most careful:

options.text: After it rains all day.
One half hour after rain stops.
During the first half hour of rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the first half hour of rain.
questions.explanation: The first half hour of rain is most dangerous. Oil from cars mixes with rain, making the road very slippery.

questions.question: When you see a flashing red traffic light, you:

options.text: Are traveling the wrong way.
Must stop as if at a stop sign.
Must wait for the light to turn green.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must stop as if at a stop sign.
questions.explanation: Treat a flashing red light like a stop sign. Stop completely at the stop line or before the crosswalk. Yield to all traffic and pedestrians.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should never:

options.text: Change lanes inside an intersection.
Look over your shoulder to check blind spots.
Check for other drivers in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes inside an intersection.
questions.explanation: Never change lanes in an intersection. Always check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder and watch for other drivers.

questions.question: If you don't see a gap when entering the freeway, you should:

options.text: Keep your speed and force other drivers to make room.
Slow down on the ramp and wait for a gap.
Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for a gap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down on the ramp and wait for a gap.
questions.explanation: Slow down on the ramp to wait for a gap. Don't stop at the end of the ramp or you won't have room to speed up before entering the freeway.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No U-turn.
No turning.
No left turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a U-turn. You cannot turn around to go in the opposite direction at this location.

questions.question: What does this yellow warning sign mean?

options.text: You are approaching a school or school crosswalk.
Slow down, drive with caution, and watch for children.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: This sign warns drivers near schools to slow down, drive carefully, and watch for children.

questions.question: When driving at night, you should:

options.text: Always use your high beams.
Look directly at the headlights of an oncoming vehicle.
Increase your following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: Driving at night is harder because you cannot see as well. You cannot judge speed and distance as easily. Increase your following distance to help prevent a collision if the car in front stops suddenly.

questions.question: You exit the freeway on a ramp that curves downhill. You should:

options.text: Slow to a safe speed before the curve.
Slow to the posted speed limit for the freeway.
Wait until you have entered the curve to begin braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow to a safe speed before the curve.
questions.explanation: Always slow down before entering a curve. You may not see hazards ahead. Braking in a curve can cause your vehicle to skid.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: You must turn right.
No right turns permitted.
Right turns permitted on a red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turns permitted.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right. It is illegal to turn right at this location.

questions.question: How do you yield to an emergency vehicle using its siren and flashing lights?

options.text: Drive to the right edge of the road and stop.
Move to the right lane and drive slowly until it passes.
Stop immediately, even if you are in an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right edge of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: You must yield to any emergency vehicle using its siren and flashing lights. Drive to the right edge and stop, but do not stop in an intersection. You can go again after the emergency vehicle passes.

questions.question: Why should you not use high beams when driving in fog or mist?

options.text: The light will reflect back into your eyes.
Approaching vehicles might not see you.
Vehicles behind you may follow too closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light will reflect back into your eyes.
questions.explanation: In fog or mist, do not use high beams. The light bounces back and makes it harder for you to see.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing red light?

options.text: Slow down and yield the right-of-way.
Slow down and drive carefully through.
Come to a complete stop, check traffic, and go when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop, check traffic, and go when safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, and then go when it is safe.

questions.question: In winter weather, maintain a following distance of at least:

options.text: Two seconds.
Three seconds.
Four seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Four seconds.
questions.explanation: In winter weather, keep a four-second following distance. Watch the car ahead pass a landmark and count to four. If you reach the same landmark before four, you are too close.

questions.question: When is a U-turn not permitted?

options.text: In a parking lot.
On or near any curve or hill.
On a straight road with a clear view for 500 feet in both directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: On or near any curve or hill.
questions.explanation: Never turn around on or near a curve or hill. You may not see oncoming traffic or pedestrians and could cause a collision.

questions.question: Your car's rear end starts skidding to the left. What should you do?

options.text: Steer to the right.
Steer to the left.
Tap your brakes lightly and shift into neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer to the left.
questions.explanation: When your car skids, take your foot off the brake. Steer in the direction you want to go. If the rear is skidding left, steer left. This straightens out your car.

questions.question: Your car starts to skid. What should you do?

options.text: Brake lightly.
Stay off the brakes.
Brake abruptly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay off the brakes.
questions.explanation: Do not brake during a skid. Braking can make the skid worse.

questions.question: Which statement is true about work zones on the road?

options.text: Fines are the same in work zones as in regular traffic areas.
You must slow down for the cone zone.
Slow down only if you see workers.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must slow down for the cone zone.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be ready to stop near road equipment. Driving slowly through work zones keeps drivers, pedestrians, bicyclists, and workers safe.

questions.question: You reach an intersection but cannot see to the side clearly. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and look both ways.
Keep your speed and look both ways.
Stop, then move forward slowly until you can see clearly both ways.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then move forward slowly until you can see clearly both ways.
questions.explanation: Slow down when you approach an intersection. If you cannot see clearly, stop completely. Then inch forward until you can see traffic from both directions.

questions.question: Bad weather makes it hard to see. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to get off the road faster.
Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.
Stay farther behind other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind other cars.
questions.explanation: When you cannot see well due to darkness or bad weather, increase the distance between your car and the car ahead. This gives you more time to react to dangers.

questions.question: A bicyclist is making a left turn. What can they do?

options.text: Use the left lane.
Cut through all lanes.
Wait on the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the left lane.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists ride with traffic on the road. You should expect to see bicyclists in the left lane when they are turning left.

questions.question: You park uphill on a two-way road with no curb. Which way do you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Straight ahead
Right, toward the side of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the side of the road
questions.explanation: When parking uphill or downhill on a road with no curb, turn your wheels toward the road edge. This way, if your brakes fail, your car rolls away from traffic.

questions.question: A red arrow pointing right on a traffic light means you may:

options.text: Turn right after slowing down and checking for traffic.
Not turn right until the light turns green.
Turn right after coming to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not turn right until the light turns green.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means stop. You must stay stopped until a green light or green arrow appears. Do not turn against a red arrow.

questions.question: You park downhill on a two-way road with no curb. Which way do you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Straight ahead
Right, toward the side of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the side of the road
questions.explanation: When parking downhill on any road, or uphill on a road with no curb, turn your wheels toward the road edge. Your car will roll away from traffic if the brakes fail. When parking uphill on a road with a curb, turn wheels toward the center so the car rolls into the curb.

questions.question: When parking next to a curb, when should you use your turn signals?

options.text: Only when pulling away from the curb.
When pulling next to the curb, but not when leaving.
When pulling next to the curb and when leaving.

questions.correctAnswerText: When pulling next to the curb and when leaving.
questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal when pulling next to a curb or when leaving it.
